''Medicago tinei'' Loj. & Poj. }} '''''Medicago arabica''''', the '''spotted medick''', '''spotted burclover''', '''heart clover''', is a [[flowering plant]] in the pea and bean family [[Fabaceae]]. ==Description== It is a sprawling plant with a height of {{Convert|20–60|cm|4=0}}. It usually has spotted trifoliate leaves, but the number of [[Leaflet (botany)|leaflets]] per leaf can sometimes be different. The flowers are pale yellow and appear spring and summer. The fruits are [[Legume|legumes]], strangely coiled and sharply spiny.{{Cite book|last=Preston-Mafham|first=Rod|title=Sea shore|publisher=[CollinsGem]|year=2004|isbn=978-0-00-717859-9}} ==Distribution and habitat== It is native to the Mediterranean basin but is found throughout the world, usually on clifftop grasslands and grassy places. It forms a symbiotic relationship with the bacterium ''[[Sinorhizobium medicae]]'', which is capable of [[nitrogen fixation]]. ==Uses== Due to its nitrogen fixation, it is sometimes considered a useful cover crop to restore soil nutrients by farmers in its native range, though it is also weedy and can thus be a nuisance. It is edible both for livestock and humans, and attracts pollinators. It also has been used in traditional medicine for possible diuretic, expectorant, and anti-inflammatory properties.{{cite web | title=Spotted Medick: Learn About Its Characteristics, Benefits & How to Grow It | website=Wild Flower Web | date=2023-06-30 | url=http://www.wildflowerweb.co.uk/plant/1782/spotted-medick | access-date=2026-04-20}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q159140}} [[Category:Medicago|arabica]] [[Category:Flora of Lebanon and Syria]] [[Category:Flora of the Arabian Peninsula]] [[Category:Flora of Egypt]] [[Category:Flora of Malta]] {{Trifolieae-stub}}
